scenes.headline: Creating DataFrames
scenes.subtitle: Turning in-memory data into a distributed, structured table.
scenes.narration: A DataFrame is Spark's distributed table of rows and named columns, and there are several easy ways to create one.

scenes.headline: Ways to create one
items: From a Python list of tuples with column names
From a Pandas DataFrame for quick prototyping
With an explicit schema for type safety
By reading a file, which we cover separately
scenes.narration: You can build a DataFrame from a Python list of tuples with column names, or from a Pandas DataFrame for quick prototyping. You can also supply an explicit schema for type safety, or create one by reading a file.

scenes.headline: Two quick ways
scenes.code:
data = [(1, "Alice"), (2, "Bob")]
df = spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name"])

from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, IntegerType, StringType
schema = StructType([StructField("id", IntegerType()), StructField("name", StringType())])
df2 = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
scenes.narration: First we create a DataFrame from a list of tuples, letting Spark infer the types from column names. Then we define an explicit schema with StructType, which gives us precise control over the types instead of relying on inference.

scenes.headline: From data to DataFrame
scenes.narration: Your local Python or Pandas data goes through createDataFrame and becomes a distributed DataFrame, ready for transformations across the cluster.

scenes.text: Define a schema for production data — inference is convenient but can guess wrong.
scenes.narration: For production pipelines, define an explicit schema; inference is convenient for exploration but can occasionally guess the wrong type.
